encode.name: o and m are Encode's: a control given with them sends neither, and o=z only when it compresses
o given with a payload that compresses: o=z goes out once, if at all

decode.name: an ok reply to place carries c and r
BEL ends a message as ST does; a reply to res has no s
error replies carry the code, the detail when there is one, and, answering a delta, the op at fault (SPEC §3.6, §6.1)
the reply to q carries the capabilities, the cell's size in CSS pixels as the host sends it
capabilities: features, and the host's version
a capability of another type: the capabilities do not decode, and the reply stands (SDK.md §3.9)
fields a reader does not know are skipped, whatever their type: an array, a float, bin, a time, an extension no one defines (SDK.md §2.7)
click: the value of the element, if it has one
click on a link: href and url, no t; url absent when there is none
change, input and submit
input, change and caret carry the control's rev, and input and caret the selection, its anchor then its caret, in bytes of UTF-8 (SPEC §6.4, §9)
an a=field the user beat is ESTALE, with the control's rev as the detail, in decimal (SPEC §3.6, §6.4)
a submit's field that is not a string: the detail does not decode, and the event stands
press, focus and blur carry no detail
a caps event carries the cell's size in CSS pixels as floats, and belongs to no surface; fit carries the rows
drags carry the cell and the modifiers held, as bits
a number of cells sent as a float: the detail does not decode, and the event stands
a drag of an element with steps carries x and y, 0 a step like any other; one the detail leaves out is absent (SPEC §9.1)
a drag's tx and ty are the pointer's step in a t with drop, beside x and y in the element dragged; one the detail leaves out is absent (SPEC §9.1)
hover carries the cell, or out
view carries each element in view by its id, with its area, and whether the document shows its end; another kind's is not read
a view with an area that is not one does not decode, and the event stands: a cell sent as a float, or the areas as an array
a view's area that lacks a field leaves its element out; with no in, no element is in view, and with no end, the end is not shown
an event of a kind the program does not know is an event all the same
a key the program does not know is kept, and changes nothing
chunks are joined before their base64 is decoded, wherever they split it
another OSC between chunks does not interrupt them
a message that interrupts a chunked one aborts it, and is decoded as usual
a malformed message that interrupts a chunked one makes two malformed messages (SPEC §3.7)
a continuation with nothing before it is malformed
a sequence with no terminator decodes as one with it
base64 without padding, and with whitespace, decodes; stray bytes are malformed
controls are strict: a duplicate key, an empty control, a value outside ASCII
other OSCs, and other numbers, are not hotty's
click and press carry the element's area; another kind's is not read
click and press carry the modifiers held as bits; none leaves them out (SPEC §9)
a body is one msgpack map: another value, a map cut short, or bytes after it, do not decode, and the message stands
a body nested more than 32 levels deep does not decode, the body's map being the first (SDK.md §3.9)

a body that holds, anywhere, what no host sends does not decode: a nil, a key that is not a string or is given twice in one map, a string that is not UTF-8, an int past 2^53 − 1, a timestamp of another size, nanoseconds of a whole second, or seconds past 2^53 − 1 (SDK.md §3.9)

a field a reader knows holding another kind of value than its type does not decode, as msgpack tells kinds apart: bin for a string, an array for a map, a map for an array, a timestamp for a map, an extension for a bool or a string (SPEC §3.3, SDK.md §3.9)
any of msgpack's forms of a type is that type: ints of any size, a float of 32 bits, long strings, arrays and maps (SPEC §3.3)
a message that decodes to more than the Decoder's max is malformed; one of max bytes is not (SDK.md §3.6)
zlib that inflates past max is malformed, and inflating stops there (SDK.md §3.6)
a chunked message past max is malformed once: its further chunks are dropped, up to its last, and the next message decodes (SPEC §3.4, SDK.md §3.6)
a chunked message past max that another interrupts is counted once (SDK.md §3.6)
a click's count is its place in a run of clicks: 1 when the detail has none, and none for another kind (SPEC §9)
features lists count: a repeated click carries its count (SPEC §4, §9); absent, it does not
command: an edit command with its key, which belongs to no surface (SPEC §10.6)
command: a paste carries the clipboard's text
command: from a menu, no key; an empty text is text
command: a detail with no name is no command
caps: the capabilities that changed, and only those (SPEC §4)
the capabilities' mod, edit and features (SPEC §4)
a limit that is not an int fails the capabilities (SPEC §3.3)

scan.name: keys around a hotty message pass; the message comes out whole
BEL ends a message as ST does
other OSCs, other numbers and CSI keys pass unchanged
a lone ESC at the end is held until the stream ends
a hotty message cut short is held, and dropped as malformed at the end
an ESC that does not end a hotty message drops it, and begins what follows
a hotty message longer than 64 KiB is dropped, up to its end
DA1 answers come out on their own
other answers that begin as DA1 does pass

detect.name: a host: its reply, then the DA1 behind it
not a host: a DA1 with no reply, then 150 ms
a DA1 before the reply may answer an earlier question: a reply within 150 ms wins
silence: not a host at 1500 ms
a reply with another n, ok or an error, is not detection's
an error that answers the query, such as EVERSION: a host this program cannot use, text at once, and done when the DA1 behind it arrives (SPEC §4)
an error of another code that answers the query is no host either, and with no DA1 behind it, done 300 ms later
capabilities that do not decode, such as a 0.1 host's JSON: text (SPEC §4)
capabilities that name a version the SDK does not speak: text (SPEC §4)
capabilities that name no version: text (SPEC §4)
with Late, a late reply that is an error or names another version changes nothing; the first that makes the terminal a host is the late answer (SPEC §4)
a reply with no DA1 behind it: done 300 ms later
the 300 ms end at 1500 ms all the same
a reply that comes too late is taken, and changes nothing
with Late, the first reply after the state is text is a late answer: the terminal is a host from then on, and a second reply changes nothing (SPEC §4)
a DA1 at the grace period's end comes too late
the input ends: what is decided stays, and nothing decided is not a host
the input ends after the reply: a host, done

keys.name: a capital is shift with its letter
text is a key for each character
a grapheme cluster is one character
C0 controls are ctrl with a letter
HT, CR, ESC and DEL are tab, enter, escape and backspace
ESC at the end of the input is escape
ESC before a key adds Alt
ESC before DEL is alt+backspace, before a control ctrl+alt
ESC before ESC is alt+escape, before a space alt+space
ESC O alone is alt+shift+o: a capital letter is shift with it
the arrows, as CSI and as SS3
xterm's modifiers on Home, End and the ~ keys
the kitty protocol: ctrl with a letter, and ctrl+shift with one
the kitty protocol: Enter, Backspace, Tab and Escape with modifiers
the kitty protocol: Super and Meta are super; Hyper and the locks name no modifier
the kitty protocol: a character with Shift is the shifted key, else the text, else the capital
the kitty protocol: event types; a release is no key
a modifier field below 2 is no modifier
a sequence the table does not name is no key
the kitty protocol: its keypad's codes name what a legacy terminal sends for the key; its modifier keys, and codes it has no name for here, are no key (SPEC §10.4)
a code that is a capital is its letter: with Shift, shift and the letter; without, the small letter, as Caps Lock makes it (SPEC §10.4)
the kitty protocol: the base layout key names nothing; the key is its code's (SPEC §10.4)
